answer: Correlation is configured on the source's correlation config (Accounts > Correlation in the UI; GET/PUT /beta/sources/{id}/correlation-config). Each entry pairs an identity attribute with an account attribute (attributeAssignments: property, value/accountAttribute, operation EQ, matchMode). During aggregation ISC evaluates the pairs in order and the account is correlated to the identity on the first pair that yields a unique match; if a pair matches multiple identities it is skipped/treated as ambiguous and the next pair is tried. Matching is generally case-insensitive exact equality; empty account values do not match. If no pair matches (and no Correlation rule assigns one), the account stays uncorrelated. For an authoritative source an uncorrelated account creates a new identity; for a non-authoritative source it stays in the Uncorrelated Accounts list and must be correlated manually (UI or PUT /v3/accounts/{id} with identityId) or by fixing data/config and re-aggregating. A Correlation rule (cloud rule, attached via correlationRule) can replace or complement the attribute pairs.

Normal (optimized/delta) aggregation only reprocesses accounts whose source data changed since the last run, so unchanged accounts are not re-evaluated against the new correlation config and stay uncorrelated. Fix: run an unoptimized aggregation, i.e. disable optimization - in the UI via the aggregation option to 'disable optimization' or via API POST /beta/sources/{sourceId}/load-accounts (or v3 /v2024 equivalent) with form field disableOptimization=true. That forces every account to be reprocessed, including correlation. Also ensure the identity attributes used in correlation are populated (identities refreshed) and values match exactly. Alternatively correlate remaining ones manually or via account PUT with identityId.

The account delete threshold (source setting deleteThreshold, default 10%, configurable in source Account Aggregation settings) protects against mass deletion: if an aggregation would remove more than that percentage of the source's existing accounts, the aggregation is stopped/fails with an error and no accounts are deleted, so a bad feed or empty file cannot wipe accounts and trigger cascading lifecycle changes. Only full account aggregations can delete accounts (accounts missing from the full feed are removed); delta/partial aggregations and single-account aggregations (e.g. reload account) do not delete missing accounts, and entitlement aggregations affect entitlements not accounts. For an intentional large cleanup you temporarily raise the threshold (e.g. PATCH /v3/sources/{id} /deleteThreshold) and rerun, then restore it. Authoritative-source deletions are the most dangerous since they can remove identities.

Create profile attributes are evaluated in the order they appear in the provisioning policy fields, and a static Velocity value can only reference fields already computed earlier in the policy (or identity attributes). Because uid (Create Unique Account ID generator) is defined below mail, $uid is not yet resolved when mail is built, so you get a literal/empty value. Fix: move the uid field above mail in the create profile (field order in the /v3/sources/{id}/provisioning-policies/CREATE fields array), then reference it as $uid. Also note the generator may retry for uniqueness; dependent fields must come after it. Alternatively compute mail from identity attributes with a transform/generator instead of Velocity.

Attribute sync pushes identity attribute values to accounts on target sources when identity attributes change (configured per source in Attribute Sync, mapping identity attribute to account attribute; source must support ENABLE/provisioning, i.e. connector with sync support). Limits: it only works on direct connectors supporting provisioning (not flat-file/delimited unless via ticket/SIM); only single-valued attributes, no multi-valued; it is triggered by identity refresh when the identity attribute value changes, not periodically reconciled for arbitrary account drift; it cannot sync attributes that are account-correlation or naming attributes on some connectors (e.g. distinguishedName/AD rename require special handling); it does not apply to disabled sync when an identity is uncorrelated; and there is a global and per-source toggle. The first enablement does not mass-sync all existing differences automatically (it only syncs on change; a full sync can be run). Changes made directly on the account are overwritten at the next sync. Values must be passed via identity attributes, transforms on the account attribute aren't applied.

Use the source schedules API: POST /beta/sources/{sourceId}/schedules (also v2024/v2025) with body {"type": "ACCOUNT_AGGREGATION", "cronExpression": "0 0 2 * * ?"} and separately {"type": "GROUP_AGGREGATION", "cronExpression": "..."} for entitlements. List with GET /beta/sources/{id}/schedules, get/update/delete with GET/PATCH/DELETE /beta/sources/{id}/schedules/{scheduleType}. Cron is Quartz-style (seconds first) in UTC. To run on demand rather than schedule: POST /v3/sources/{id}/load-accounts (or /beta) and POST /beta/sources/{id}/load-entitlements. Requires scope like idn:sources:manage.

Check: (1) the source's connector supports native change detection (e.g. AD, Entra, some others) and the source is direct (not delimited); (2) NCD is enabled on the source with the right operations selected (account create/update/delete) and attributes - for updates only the configured attributes (entitlements/selected attrs) generate events; (3) detection only happens during account aggregation - changes must have been made directly on the target (not by ISC provisioning, which is excluded), and an aggregation must run after the change; optimized aggregation still detects changes, but the first aggregation after enabling builds the baseline; (4) the Native Change event trigger (idn:account-native-change? 'Native Change Account Created/Updated/Deleted' triggers) has an active subscription or a workflow using it, with correct filter; (5) uncorrelated accounts may not be included. Look at subscription testing and trigger invocation status (GET /beta/trigger-invocations/status).

The create profile is the provisioning policy with usageType CREATE: GET /v3/sources/{sourceId}/provisioning-policies/CREATE, replace it with PUT /v3/sources/{sourceId}/provisioning-policies/CREATE (full body: name, usageType, fields[] with name, transform, attributes, isRequired, type, isMultiValued), or partially update with PATCH (JSON Patch, Content-Type application/json-patch+json) e.g. op replace on /fields/2/transform. If none exists, create with POST /v3/sources/{sourceId}/provisioning-policies. There is also bulk-update POST /v3/sources/{id}/provisioning-policies/bulk-update. A source can have only one policy per usageType, so only one CREATE policy; other usage types (UPDATE, ENABLE, DISABLE, DELETE, CHANGE_PASSWORD, etc.) are separate policies.

List uncorrelated accounts with GET /v3/accounts?filters=sourceId eq "<sourceId>" and uncorrelated eq true (paginate with limit up to 250 and offset, count=true for total). Alternatively use search for accounts. To correlate, call PUT /v3/accounts/{accountId} with body {"identityId": "<identityId>"} for each account (there is no single bulk correlate endpoint in v3; loop with rate-limit handling, ~100 req/10s). In the UI you can bulk correlate via Uncorrelated Accounts by uploading a CSV correlation file (account ID/name to identity). Better long-term: fix correlation config and run an unoptimized aggregation (disableOptimization=true) so ISC correlates them automatically.

No. The features array describes what the connector actually implements; for SailPoint-supported connectors it is set by the connector/type and editing it doesn't add capability, it can cause failures or unexpected behavior (ISC would try to send provisioning plans the connector configuration isn't set up for), and it is an unsupported configuration. For JDBC, provisioning is implemented through JDBC Provision rules (connector rule JDBCProvision, uploaded via the connector rules API /beta/connector-rules and referenced in the source's connectorAttributes, e.g. provisioning rule) and enabling provisioning in the source config; once configured properly the source supports provisioning. Changing features via PATCH /v3/sources/{id} should be reserved for cases documented by SailPoint (e.g. removing features to disable behavior, or some flat-file/custom SaaS connectors), and done with care.
